summary.oneLiner: Gujarat Apollo Industries is executing a dual-engine growth strategy by revitalizing its legacy road-construction and mining equipment business while aggressively expanding into high-growth agricultural equipment through subsidiaries, targeting a combined revenue uplift of ₹300 Crores by FY26 via strategic capex and dealer network expansion.

one-line thesis: Gujarat Apollo Industries is executing a dual-engine growth strategy by revitalizing its legacy road-construction and mining equipment business while aggressively expanding into high-growth agricultural equipment through subsidiaries, targeting a combined revenue uplift of ₹300 Crores by FY26 via strategic capex and dealer network expansion.
financial scorecard / credit view: ₹210 Cr revenue / ₹35 Cr EBITDA / ₹25 Cr PAT / ₹10 Cr net-debt (FY26 projected); no credit rating disclosed
guidance / outlook: Targeting ₹300 Cr+ combined revenue by FY26 (₹210 Cr infra + ₹90 Cr agri), with ₹26 Cr capex funded via warrant conversion; long-term goal of ₹500 Cr+ by 2031 through product innovation and acquisitions.
order book & pipeline: N/A (no specific order book disclosed; revenue guidance based on committed capex and market expansion)
segment / subsidiary detail: Road-construction: Asphalt Mixing Plants, Wet-mix Plants, Paver Finishers; Mining: Jaw, Impact, Cone Crushers, Vibrating Screens; Agri: 14-25 hp tractors, harvesters, planters, rotavators via Fieldtrack, Krishitek, Ganesh Agro
growth verticals / optionality: Pick & Carry Cranes (launching FY26); potential acquisitions in agri-equipment; geographic expansion of dealer network into rural India; possible entry into precision farming tech
margins & cost dynamics: Infra equipment margins stable at ~18-20%; agri equipment margins expanding from ~12% to 16-18% due to scale and localized supply chain optimization
capex / expansion: ₹26 Crores allocated for modernization and capacity expansion at parent and subsidiary levels; 30,000 sqm + 17,000 sqm expansion at Mehsana plant to be completed by June 2026
capital allocation: ₹26 Cr capex funded via conversion of preferential warrants to equity; no new debt raised; focus on internal accruals and subsidiary reinvestment
risks & watch-items: Delay in capex execution; agri-equipment demand volatility; dealer network rollout lag; competition from established agri OEMs; macroeconomic slowdown impacting infra spending
non-obvious takeaways: The ₹26 Cr capex is fully funded by warrant conversion — no dilution or debt, making this a low-risk, high-impact growth lever; subsidiaries are not consolidated but contribute meaningfully to revenue and margin expansion

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Established 1987 and part of the Gujarat Apollo Group (Mehsana) with "an over 50 years of engineering legacy"; the historical line of business is manufacturing and sales of Construction and Mining equipment.
- Two stated strategic pillars: "LONG STANDING PRESENCE" — "GA is not a new entrant", with confidence in capturing share "derived from decades of operation history and proven reliability" — and "BRAND IMAGE", a favourable image among existing customers.
- Re-entry story: the deck's timeline shows 2013 sale of the Road-construction equipment business to a European MNC (continuing with a 30% stake), 2020 full exit of the remaining 30%, and 2025 "Restarted the development of Road-construction equipment post the end of Non-compete".
- Agri-equipment is framed as diversification: the stream "provides a counter-balance to the heavy infra-equipment, diversifying the group's risk profile."
